name: WinVidCompress
summary: A local Windows video compressor built with PowerShell and FFmpeg. Drag files or folders onto the launcher to create consistent H.264/AAC MP4 viewing copies.
requirements: Windows; recorded workstation tests use Windows 11 Pro x64.
Windows PowerShell 5.1 (BAT launcher) or supported stable PowerShell 7 (direct PS1).
Separately supplied FFmpeg and FFprobe with libx264, AAC, MP4/faststart, scale and JSON/CSV probing support.
An available writable output directory and sufficient free space; no administrator account required.
tested_platforms: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 x64; Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9444 Desktop and PowerShell 7.6.6 Core.
FFmpeg/FFprobe 2026-10-04-git-a35c879992 essentials Windows build; tests describe this build, not every dependency build.
Prior Windows CI Targeted tests run on windows-2025 in both PowerShell hosts; separate Full/manual/release evidence applies.
setup: Extract the scripts together; read README and keep the offline user guides and policies.
Obtain FFmpeg/FFprobe from a Windows provider linked by FFmpeg's download page and follow the provider's integrity checks.
Use an existing PATH installation or place both executables adjacent to the scripts; PATH takes precedence.
Run -CheckEnvironment, then separate -WhatIf and first-copy commands with explicit disposable inputs and an existing output folder.
Use the four-item menu or drag/drop launcher for everyday sequential batches; default output is flat with safe collision renaming.
privacy: Compression runs on the user's device. No application uploads, telemetry, accounts or automatic dependency downloads.
Explicit UNC inputs and outputs can access network shares.
Config, local logs, manifests and outputs can contain private paths, filenames and metadata. Review before sharing.

measured_examples.label: Four-second synthetic pattern and tone: FFV1/PCM source to the fixed H.264/AAC profile, three local runs.
measured_examples.scope: Synthetic lossless input, not a typical already-compressed interview. Real measured bytes and local warm-cache timings; results vary and valid outputs can grow. Playback NotRun; structural validation is not perceptual proof.

known_limitations: Lossy viewing copies are not archival masters. Keep originals and review outputs; a valid output can be larger.
Detected HDR is refused; no tone mapping. Ambiguous colour warns. Other video/audio streams, subtitles, data and attachments are omitted and reported.
BAT paths containing variable-shaped percent segments such as %PATH% require literal-path menu or direct PS1 routes. Outer CMD delayed expansion and the CMD command-line limit also apply.
Oriented height cap is 1080 with even dimensions, no crop or upscale; width is not capped at 1920.
Compatible source tags may remain. Compression does not sanitize private metadata.
Structural validation does not prove full visual/audio integrity. Bounded recorded owner playback checks are not whole-original, HDR or every-player acceptance.
Remote SMB/disconnection, arbitrary filesystems/long paths, power loss, hostile substitution, console close and detached descendants have broader unverified limits.
Final release-source reconstruction, candidate acceptance, browser/MOTW, fresh-profile and default-Videos first launch remain separate distribution limits.
Unsigned, tool-only unpublished candidate. Checksums detect changed bytes, not publisher authenticity or guaranteed safety. FFmpeg has separate build-dependent license terms.
